questions.question: If N = 2³ × 3², then what are the positive factors of N?
questions.solution:
A number to be a positive factor of (2³ × 3²) it should be a positive factor of both 2 and 3.

Prime factorisation

5 = 5

8 = 2 × 2 × 2

12 = 2 × 2 × 3

20 = 2 × 2 × 5

Out of the above numbers, 12 is only one with factors both 2 and 3

∴ 12 in positive factor of 2³ × 3².

questions.question: What is the least common multiple of 24, 48 and 72?
questions.solution:
Listing the prime factor of each number

24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3

72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

Multiply each factor the greatest number of times it occurs in any of the numbers.

48 has 4 2s, 72 has 2 3s. This gives us 144, the smallest number that can be divided evenly by 24, 48 and 72

On dividing 12121 by 10, we get a remainder 1.

questions.question: X, Y, and Z together can complete a work in 20 days. Y and Z can complete the same work in 30 days. In how many days can X complete the same work alone?
questions.solution:
Work done by X, Y, and Z in one day = 1/20

Work done by Y and Z in one day = 1/30

⇒ Work done by X in one day = (1/20) – (1/30) = 1/60

∴ X can complete the work alone in 60 days.

questions.question: U, V and W together can complete a work in 10 days. If U alone can complete the work in 20 days and V alone can complete the work in 30 days, then in how many days W alone can complete the work?
questions.solution:
1 day work of U, V and W = 1/10

1 day work of U = 1/20

1 day work of V = 1/30(3)

⇒ 1 day work of W = (1/10) - (1/20) - (1/30) = 1/60

∴ W can complete the work in 60 days.

questions.question: If the surface area of cube is 384 cm², then what is the volume (in cm³) of the cube?
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the cube be a cm

Surface area of cube = 6 × a²

⇒ 6 × a² = 384

⇒ a² = 64

⇒ a = 8

∴ Volume of cube = a³ = 8³ = 512 cm³

questions.question: Average weight of P and Q is 32 kg. Average weight of Q and R is 43 kg. Average weight of P and R is 51 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of P, Q and R?
questions.solution:
∵ Average weight of P and Q is 32 kg

⇒ Sum of their weight = 2 × 32 = 64

⇒ P + Q = 64 kg (1)

Similarly,

Q + R = 86 kg (2)

P + R = 102 kg (3)

Adding equation (1), (2) and (3)

2P + 2Q + 2R = 64 + 86 + 102 = 252

⇒ P + Q + R = 126 kg

∴ Average weight of P, Q and R = (P + Q + R)/3 = 126/3 = 42 kg

questions.question: If cost price is Rs. 50 less than the selling price and profit is 10%, then what is the selling price (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Selling price = S.P

Cost price = C.P

According to question,

C.P = S.P - 50

⇒ S.P - C.P = 50

Profit percentage = (S.P - CP) × 100/CP

⇒ (50 × 100)/C.P = 10

⇒ C.P = (50 × 100)/10 = 500

⇒ S.P - 50 = 500

⇒ S.P = 550

questions.question: If profit is 1/9th of selling price, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Selling price = S.P

Cost price = C.P

According to question,

Profit = S.P/9

⇒ S.P - C.P = S.P/9

⇒ 9 S.P - 9 C.P = S.P

⇒ S.P = 9/8 C.P

Profit percentage = [(S.P - C.P) × 100]/C.P = {(9/8 C.P - C.P) × 100}/C.P = 12.5%

A train passes two bridges of length 600 metres and 300 metres in 120 seconds and 80 seconds respectively. What is the length (in metres) of the train?
questions.solution:
Let the length of train be L m

Speed = distance/time

Distance covered by train in 120 sec = (600 + L)

Speed = (600 + L)/120(1)

Distance covered by train in 80 sec = (300 + L)

Speed = (300 + L)/80(2)

Equating equation (1) and (2)

(600 + L)/120 = (300 + L)/80

⇒ 1200 + 2L = 900 + 3L

⇒ L = 1200 - 900 = 300 m

questions.question: Raman goes office at a speed of 40 kmph and returns home at a speed of 60 kmph. What is his average speed (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
Let the distance between Raman’s office and home is x km

Speed = distance/time

Time = distance/speed

Time taken to go to office, t₁ = x/40

Time taken to return to home, t₂ = x/60

Total time taken = t₁ + t₂ = x/40 + x/60 = x/24

Total distance travelled = 2x

Average speed = total distance travelled/total time taken = (2x)/(x/24) = 48 kmph

questions.question: A certain amount is invested in a scheme of simple interest. It amounts to Rs. 3096 in 6 years and Rs. 3744 in 9 years. What is the rate of interest (in percentage)?
questions.solution:
Simple interest = S.I = (principle × rate × time)/100

Let the principle be p

Rate of interest be r

After 6 years,

Amount = p + S.I

⇒ p + (p × r × 6)/100 = 3096

⇒ 100p + 6 × r × p - 309600 = 0(1)

After 9 years,

Amount = p + S.I

⇒ p + (p × r × 9)/100 = 3744

⇒ 100p + 9 × r × p - 374400 = 0(2)

Solving equation (1) and (2)

p = 1800 and r = 12

∴ rate of interest = 12%

questions.question: What is the average number of students from year 2000 to 2002?
questions.solution:
Average number of students from year 2000 to 2002 = (number of student in 2000 + number of students in 2001 + number of students in 2002)/3

⇒ Average number of students from year 2000 to 2002 = (1000 + 1200 + 1400)/3 = 1200

Solution:

Total number of students in year 2002 and 2003 = 1400 + 1500 = 2900

questions.question: What is the difference between the total number of students in year 2004 and 2000?
questions.solution:
Difference between the total number of students in year 2004 and 2000 = (number of students in year 2004) - (number of students in year 2000)

Difference between the total number of students in year 2004 and 2000 = 1600 - 1000 = 600

questions.question: Students in year 2003 is how much percent more than the students in year 2000?
questions.solution:
Difference between the total number of students in year 2003 and 2000 = 1500 - 1000 = 500

Percentage difference in number of students = (500 × 100)/1000 = 50%
